reasons: The empty-category case sends every uncategorised fact to the first pillar in the single-fact routing helper, which hides the keyword routing.
Keyword matching by substring can misroute facts.
The rule that an empty result must stop deck production is only in a comment, not enforced in this file.
No tests were visible for this file.

terms.meaning: One broad theme in the final recipe, such as cost and schedule realism.
A narrower point under a pillar, used for finer routing.
A label attached to a fact, often taken from the name of the field it came from.
Assigning a fact to a theme by searching its text for listed words.
A piece of text found inside a longer piece of text.
The fixed list of themes written into the code.
A plain data field such as status or owner, which describes a project but is not a theme.
Describes a pillar created from the data rather than from the library. Not used in this file.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File purpose and header rules
sections.what: The header comment explains the approach: themes come from the facts in each run, library themes appear only when supported, and outcome labels are never used to score pillars.
sections.why: The header states these rules directly, so they are the intended design.
sections.watch_out: The rules are documented here but are not checked by this file alone.

sections.name: ThemeSub
sections.title: Shape of a sub-point
sections.what: Describes a narrower point under a theme: an id, its wording, a reason, and a list of keywords.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: lets each theme carry finer points for routing.
sections.watch_out: Routing uses only these keyword lists, so editing them changes results directly.

sections.name: ThemeDef
sections.title: Shape of a theme
sections.what: Describes a full theme: id, name, principle, categories, keywords, sub-points, and a flag for themes made from unmatched categories.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shape is shared by library themes and derived pillars.
sections.watch_out: The inductive flag is never set to true in this file.

sections.name: THEME_LIBRARY (part 1)
sections.title: Start of the theme library
sections.what: Begins the fixed list of themes, with the first one covering definition and design readiness. Each theme has categories, keywords, a principle sentence, and sub-points.
sections.why: The comment calls it internal routing vocabulary, not a fixed output template.
sections.watch_out: Short keywords such as ore or scope can match inside longer words, so routing can be loose.

sections.name: THEME_LIBRARY (part 2)
sections.title: Cost and ownership themes
sections.what: Continues the library with the cost and schedule theme, including its sub-points, then starts the ownership and commercial theme with its categories and keywords.
sections.why: Reason not stated beyond the library's routing role.
sections.watch_out: Keywords such as fund and invest can match unrelated text.

sections.name: THEME_LIBRARY (part 3)
sections.title: Finishing the ownership theme
sections.what: Adds the funding, contracting and owner-capability sub-points and ends the ownership theme.
sections.why: Reason not stated beyond the library's routing role.
sections.watch_out: The word owner appears as both a category and a keyword, so a fact can match more than one theme.

sections.name: THEME_LIBRARY (part 4)
sections.title: Delivery and permitting themes
sections.what: Adds the workforce and ramp sub-points, ends the delivery theme, and starts the permitting, political and social-licence theme with its categories, keywords and first sub-points.
sections.why: Reason not stated beyond the library's routing role.
sections.watch_out: Broad categories such as water and land can pull in facts that are not about permitting.

sections.name: THEME_LIBRARY (part 5)
sections.title: Closing the library list
sections.what: Adds the community sub-point to the permitting theme and closes the library list.
sections.why: Reason not stated beyond the library's routing role.
sections.watch_out: Routing by category takes the first matching theme, so reordering or adding themes changes results.

sections.name: indPhrase
sections.title: Industry phrase for principles
sections.what: Builds a short phrase such as in Mining to put into theme principles, or returns nothing for generic labels.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps generic labels from making the principle sentences read awkwardly.
sections.watch_out: Only a fixed set of generic labels is recognised, so other generic wording will still appear in the text.

sections.name: METADATA_FIELD_PATHS
sections.title: Plain data fields that are not themes
sections.what: Lists plain data fields such as owner, status, and cost and schedule overrun, which must never become themes.
sections.why: The comment says these metadata fields must never create fake pillars.
sections.watch_out: A new plain data field must be added to this list, or it may be treated as a theme category.

sections.name: categoryFromFieldPath
sections.title: Turning a field path into a category
sections.what: Turns a raw field path into a category name. It returns nothing for empty paths and plain data fields, and removes the fact prefix from tagged paths.
sections.why: The comment says Compass stores thematic tags with a fact prefix, so this step extracts the tag.
sections.watch_out: Any field that is not in the plain-field list and lacks the prefix becomes a category, so new metadata fields can leak into themes.

sections.name: themeOfCategory
sections.title: Finding the theme for a category
sections.what: Returns the position of the first library theme whose category words appear in the category name, or nothing.
sections.why: Likely reason: a quick way to map each category to one theme.
sections.watch_out: The first match wins, and the check is a substring match, so short category words can match longer names.

sections.name: kwTheme
sections.title: Finding the theme from fact text
sections.what: For facts without a usable category, counts how many keywords of each theme appear in the fact text and returns the theme with the highest count.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives uncategorised facts a fallback route.
sections.watch_out: Ties go to the earlier theme, and a zero score returns nothing.

sections.name: FactLike
sections.title: Minimal fact shape
sections.what: Describes the minimum a fact needs for this file: its text and an optional category.
sections.why: Reason not stated. Likely reason: lets this file work without the full fact record.
sections.watch_out: The file does not check the types of these values at runtime.

sections.name: DerivedFramework
sections.title: Shape of the framework result
sections.what: Describes the result: the pillars, a mode label, the category-to-pillar map, a count of library themes used, and an inductive count.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives callers the full picture of how the pillars were built.
sections.watch_out: The mode label and the inductive count always have the same values here, so they carry no information.

sections.name: deriveFramework (part 1)
sections.title: Building pillars from present themes
sections.what: Counts facts per category, maps each category to a theme, routes each fact by category or by text, and counts facts per theme. It creates a pillar only for themes with at least one fact, numbered P1, P2 and so on in library order.
sections.why: The comment says a theme needs at least one routed fact, and an empty result must not be padded with an unsupported template.
sections.watch_out: Pillar numbers depend on which themes have facts, so the same theme can get a different id from one run to another.

sections.name: deriveFramework: for
sections.title: Recording the category map
sections.what: Records which category belongs to which pillar id, so later steps can route by category.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets later steps route facts without repeating the mapping.
sections.watch_out: Categories whose theme has no pillar are left out of the map.

sections.name: routeFactToPillar
sections.title: Routing one fact to a pillar
sections.what: Assigns a single fact to a pillar, first by checking its category words, then by counting keywords in its text and choosing the highest score. It returns nothing if nothing matches.
sections.why: Likely reason: the same routing rules as the framework step, for one fact at a time.
sections.watch_out: An empty category matches every pillar's words through the two-way check, so the first pillar always wins and keyword routing never runs for uncategorised facts.

sections.name: routeFactToSubDriver
sections.title: Routing one fact to a sub-point
sections.what: Picks the sub-point under a pillar whose keywords appear most often in the fact text. It returns nothing if no sub-point matches.
sections.why: The comment says that returning nothing is deliberate, so a fact is not forced into a sub-point it does not fit.
sections.watch_out: Ties keep the first sub-point, and facts with no match stay at pillar level only.

summary: Decides which broad themes, called pillars, the evidence in a run belongs to, using a fixed internal list of themes and keeping only themes that have at least one matching fact.
purpose: Organises a run's facts into themes that the deck can present, without making up themes the evidence does not support.
why: The header says pillars are worked out from the categories and text present in each run, not from a fixed template. It also says outcome labels are kept separate from themes.
how: It reads each fact's category and maps the category to a library theme by matching category words. If no category matches, it searches the fact text for the theme keywords and picks the best score. It counts facts per theme and keeps only themes with at least one fact, numbering them P1, P2 and so on. It records which category belongs to which pillar. Separate helpers route a single fact to a pillar or to a sub-point.
inputs: A list of facts, each with text and an optional category, and an optional industry label used in the wording of each theme's principle.
outputs: A result with the chosen pillars, a mode label, a map from category to pillar id, a count of library themes used, and an inductive count. The two routing helpers return a pillar id, a sub-point id, or nothing.
risks: Keyword matching checks whether a word appears inside any longer text, so short keywords like ore or fund can match unrelated words. A fact with an empty category matches the first pillar automatically in the routing helper, so keyword routing never runs for those facts. Facts with no matching category or keyword are dropped. The inductive path is declared but never used.
debug: If an expected pillar is missing, check whether any fact's category or text contains that theme's words. If a fact lands in the wrong theme, look at the keyword lists for short words that match inside other words. If routing sends uncategorised facts to the first pillar, check the empty-category case in the single-fact routing helper. If there are no pillars at all, callers must treat the empty set as insufficient evidence.
